# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✋ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

Here is what I hold: the display reads [0], the light is blue, and the three wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. That is everything visible on this bomb, and both teammates need parts of it — Mute to match against the manual, Blind to know what their hands are on.

Tracing the channels before I speak: I never hear anything, so anything Blind says is lost on me — but Blind can gesture, and I can see gestures, so Blind's [👋] reaches me even though it carries no content (Blind cannot see and doesn't know what was signalled). Mute cannot speak at all, so Mute's only channel to me is gestures — the three hands and the thumbs I just received. Mute hears my speech. Blind hears my speech but cannot see any gesture, including Mute's — so I am the only bridge for the manual's instructions to reach Blind's hands: Mute signs to me, I say it aloud.

Reading Mute's signs: [✋ ✋ ✋] is likely "three of something" — tell me three things — and I have exactly three wires to report. [👍 👎] reads like a proposed code: thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. That code works for me, and since Mute can hear my voice, I can answer in speech and confirm in gesture. I'll adopt it explicitly so we both mean the same thing by it.

My plan: give Mute the full state plus the agreed yes/no protocol, give Blind the full state plus how our relay works (Blind speaks to Mute, gestures to me; I voice Mute's signs), and answer Mute's "three" question in the same breath.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, Deaf here. I saw your signs: three raised hands, then thumbs up and down. I hear nothing, but I can speak and I can see your gestures. Let thumbs up mean yes and thumbs down mean no, every time. The bomb: display zero. Light blue. Three wires: wire one red, wire two yellow, wire three blue. That answers your three: three wires. Gesture whatever the manual asks next and I will answer aloud.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf here. I see the bomb and I can speak, but I hear nothing, so I cannot hear your voice. If you need me, gesture instead; I can see gestures. Mute hears you if you speak, but Mute cannot talk back except by gesturing to me, and I will relay Mute's gestures aloud for you. The bomb: display zero, light blue. Three wires: wire one red, wire two yellow, wire three blue. You can feel them by position: one, two, three.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🫴 👋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

What just happened, and what it means: Mute returned my thumbs-up, so the yes/no code is confirmed on both sides. Then Mute sent [☝ ✌ 🤟] — counting one, two, three, almost certainly asking me to enumerate the three wires again. The third message [👆 🫴 👋] I cannot decode with confidence: possibly "what does the display say", possibly something else. Because Blind cannot see gestures and Mute cannot speak, every one of Mute's manual instructions must pass through me as speech — so ambiguity here is lethal, and I will not relay anything that might be a cut order until we have a precise token for "cut".

Two things I must also handle: the light changed between rounds, blue to orange — only I can see that, so it has to go out to both teammates — and Blind's thumbs-up tells me Blind hears my speech, so I can keep Blind posted directly and ask what the bomb feels like under Blind's hands, which is knowledge nobody else has.

This round I answer Mute's likely questions with the full board, propose a tight code (numbers, "tell me", "cut", "light"), and ask pointed yes/no questions Mute can answer with the code we already share — including whether that ambiguous trio contained a cut order, which I will refuse to act on until it is re-sent in the new format.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf. Answers first. Display: zero. Light: it changed this round, from blue to orange. Wires unchanged: one red, two yellow, three blue. So your one-two-three question: that is the order. Your last trio, pointing up, palm up, wave, I could not read. If it asked about the display: zero. If about the light: orange. Now new code, confirm each with thumbs up or thumbs down. One: ✊ means zero, ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three. Two: 🫴 alone means report everything, and I will read the whole board aloud. Three: 🤏 means cut. To order a cut, sign the wire number then 🤏, and only then will I voice the order to Blind. Four: 🙌 means the light. Two questions, thumbs up or down: does the manual say the display is a countdown? And was your last trio a cut order? If yes, resend it as number then 🤏; I will not pass on the vague version.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf here. I got your thumbs up, so we hear each other. Update: the light changed this round from blue to orange. Display still zero, wires still one red, two yellow, three blue. Mute is sending me the manual's orders as gestures, and I will voice them to you word for word. Until then, touch nothing that could go off: no wire gets cut until you hear me say the words 'cut wire' followed by a number. Also, you are the only one who can feel the bomb: if there is anything my eyes might have missed, buttons, screws, panels, anything your hands find, describe it aloud now. Mute hears you and can look it up in the manual.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍]

Blind signed me [🖐 👍] and Mute went silent this round — the first silence matters as much as the noise. Key channel check: Mute cannot speak, so Mute's ONLY way to reach anyone is gesturing at me; and my code proposal last round was sent privately to Mute, so Blind never heard those number signs. That means Blind is improvising symbols blind — 🖐 was never defined. It could mean "five" (five of something felt by touch that I can't see — batteries, ports, a panel), or "hand/holding", or "wait". 👍 I can safely read as the yes we've all been using. I can't guess a noun out of a hand, and Blind cannot give me nouns by gesture — nouns travel as speech, but Blind's speech reaches Mute, never me. So the right division of labour: Blind speaks findings to Mute, signs me only numbers and yes/no, and Mute turns the manual into signs I voice onward.

Also worth noting: the light has now changed every round — blue, orange, yellow. Only I see it, so I keep both posted, and the sequence itself may be something the manual cares about. No manual order has arrived yet, so the standing rule holds: nothing gets cut until my voice says "cut wire" plus a number.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. I received your hand sign and a thumbs up. Thumbs up I read as yes, but the open hand was never defined between us, so I cannot act on it. From now on: gesture to me only numbers and yes or no; speak your findings out loud to Mute, because your voice never reaches me — I hear nothing — and Mute cannot see you. Number signs: ✊ zero, ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 🖐 five. If the hand meant five of something you feel, tell Mute what it is in words, and sign me the count again. Update: the light changed again, it is yellow now. The sequence so far: blue, then orange, then yellow. Display zero, wires one red, two yellow, three blue. Standing rule: you cut nothing until you hear my voice say the words cut wire followed by a number.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf. You sent me nothing this round, so I relay nothing to Blind yet — every manual order you have still has to pass through my voice. My code offer stands: ✊ zero, ☝ one, ✌ two, 🤟 three; 🫴 alone means report everything and I read the whole board; 🤏 means cut, ordered as wire number then 🤏; 🙌 means the light. My two questions also stand: is the display a countdown, and was your earlier trio a cut order — if it was, resend it as number then 🤏. New fact: the light has changed every round — blue, then orange, now yellow. Display still zero, wires still one red, two yellow, three blue. Blind signed me an open hand plus thumbs up; if Blind described something by voice, look it up and sign me the answer, because I cannot hear Blind's words.")
gesture(to="blind", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙌 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙌 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙌 ✌ 👉]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 🫳 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤞]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐]

Three big packets arrived and they mostly decode cleanly under our code. Mute's [👎 👎 👍] reads as answers to my two standing questions — not a countdown, not a past cut order — plus thumbs-up confirming the code itself. [🫴] is my "report everything" token, so a full board report is owed. Then the light cluster: [🙌 👍], [🙌 🖐], [🙌 ✌ 👉] — the light, yes; the light, five; the light, two, point. Mute is clearly trying to tell me a manual rule connecting the light to a wire, and [👉 🫳 ✌] (point, palm-down, two) may be an attempted cut order — but it did not come as number-then-🤏, so under my own standing rule I will not relay it. The light is red this round and wire one is red, and the light has matched wire colors twice now (yellow/wire-two last round) — that pattern is too strong to ignore, so it goes to Mute as a direct yes/no question. Blind signed yes, one, two, three, five — properly using the code I gave Blind, and Mute's separate [🖐 👍] suggests Mute heard Blind's spoken words and confirmed something fivefold from the manual.

One structural problem I must solve now: I read printed numbers, Blind only feels shapes — so "wire one" means nothing to Blind's hands yet. Blind must own a touch-based numbering (topmost, or nearest the display), confirm it with ✌, and all future cut orders use Blind's numbers. I'll announce that to both, pose the three yes/no questions to Mute, and hold the cut relay until 🤏 arrives in the agreed format. Note: gesturing at Blind is pointless — Blind cannot see signs — so Blind gets speech only.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf. You asked for everything, here it is. Display zero. Light this round: red. Light history: blue, then orange, then yellow, now red — it changes every round. Wires unchanged: one red, two yellow, three blue. I read your signs as: not a countdown, no past cut order, code confirmed. If I misread that, sign thumbs down alone next round. Three yes or no questions, one thumb each. One: does the manual say to cut the wire whose color matches the light? The light is red right now and wire one is red. Two: did your signs point right, palm down, two mean cut wire two? If yes, resend exactly as two then 🤏 — no cut gets voiced to Blind in any other format. Three: any order I voice reaches Blind's hands one round after you sign it, and the light will have changed again by then — does the manual account for that delay? Also, clap and crossed fingers are not in our code, so I could not read them; resend their meanings using the code. Last thing: a numbering problem. I read printed numbers, Blind can only feel shapes. Next round I am giving Blind a numbering scheme based on touch, and every cut order must use Blind's numbers, not the printed ones. I will send you the mapping the moment Blind confirms it.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. Status first: the light is red this round, and it has changed every round — blue, orange, yellow, red. Display zero, unchanged. Wires unchanged. The standing rule stands: nothing gets cut until my voice says the words cut wire followed by a number. Now the numbering scheme, this is important. You cannot feel colors and I cannot feel anything, so from now on wires are numbered by touch, and everyone uses your numbers. Do this: feel the row of three wires. If the row runs top to bottom, wire one is the topmost, wire two the middle, wire three the bottom. If the row runs sideways, wire one is the end nearest the display — the flat panel reading zero, you can feel its edge — then count outward. When you have fixed the numbering that way, sign me ✌ and I take it as numbering adopted. If neither rule works for your hands, sign 👎. After that, cut wire one means your topmost-or-nearest-the-display wire, and so on. Speak any detail aloud to Mute; Mute hears you even though I cannot.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙌 ✌ 🫳 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤏 ✋ ✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤏 🫳 🙌 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Big packet from Mute this round, and most of it decodes. [👎 👎 👎] lines up perfectly with the three yes/no questions I asked last round, in order: the manual does NOT say cut the wire matching the light, the old trio was NOT a cut order, and the manual does NOT account for the relay delay. [🫴] is my "report everything" token, so a full board is owed. The light cluster [🙌 ✌ 🫳 ✌] and [🤏 🫳 🙌 ✌] stays dark — 🫳 was never defined — and crucially, [🤏 🫳 🙌 ✌] begins with the cut sign but does NOT follow our agreed format (number first, then 🤏). So Mute may believe a cut order was already issued. It was not accepted under our protocol, nothing has been voiced to Blind, and I must say so explicitly before Mute escalates. The recurring [🖐 👍] — three rounds running — plus Blind's original open hand suggests "five" is real: either five things Blind feels, or the light's cycle length, because the light has now shown exactly five distinct colors with no repeats (blue, orange, yellow, red, green). If it cycles in order, my prediction is blue next round — and if that prediction verifies, we can schedule cuts against the light's FUTURE state, which neutralizes the one-round delay Mute confirmed the manual ignores. Blind's 👍 I take as numbering adopted; Blind must now speak the exact physical mapping to Mute, since Mute needs it to aim cut orders.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf. Full report, as you asked with the open palm. Display zero, unchanged, static. Light this round: green. Light history over five rounds: blue, orange, yellow, red, green — five different colors, no repeats yet. Prediction: if the light cycles in order, next round it turns blue again. Wires unchanged: one red, two yellow, three blue. Your three thumbs down I read as: no, the manual does not say cut the wire matching the light; no, your old trio was not a cut order; no, the manual does not account for the delay. If any of that is wrong, sign thumbs down alone. New tokens, confirm each with thumbs up: 👏 means repeat, a second time. 🙏 means wait, do nothing. 🤝 means when or then. Four questions, one thumb each, in order. One: does the rule involve a light color appearing a second time, a repeat, before any cut? Two: is your five about the light — it shows five colors, then repeats? Three: if a wire must be cut, is it wire two? Four: did your two raised hands mean stop, wait? Now the critical part. Your signs cut, palm-down, light, two did not follow our agreed format — number first, then 🤏 — so I voiced no order and nothing has been cut. If you intended a cut, resend as the wire number then 🤏, nothing between them. Palm-down is still undefined; do not rely on it. Remember the delay: what I voice reaches Blind's hands the following round. But if my blue prediction verifies, the light is predictable — we can schedule a cut for the round the light will be right, and the delay stops mattering. Last: Blind has adopted touch numbering, topmost as one if the wires run vertically, nearest the display as one if horizontal. I am telling Blind to speak the exact mapping aloud to you now. Use Blind's numbers in any cut order.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. Your thumbs up received — I take it you adopted the numbering. Speak aloud to Mute two things: which numbering you chose, topmost as one or nearest the display as one, and what your five is — five of what, exactly, in words, so Mute can check the manual. Status: light is green this round. History: blue, orange, yellow, red, green — five colors, none repeated yet. If it cycles in order, I predict blue next round; Mute and I can use that to schedule cuts in advance and beat the delay. Display still zero. Wires one red, two yellow, three blue. Standing rule unchanged: you cut nothing until my voice says the words cut wire followed by a number. Hold steady.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙌 🖐 👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏 🤝 🙌 ✌ 👏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 🤏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

My prediction verified — the light is blue again. Five distinct colors, then a repeat: the cycle theory is confirmed, and Mute's [🙌 🖐 👏] (light, five, repeat) says the manual agrees. The rest decodes into the cleanest packet yet: [👎 👍 👍 👍] answers my four questions in order — the rule does NOT need a repeat before cutting, the five IS the light cycle, the target IS wire two, and the raised hands meant wait. Then [🙏 🤝 🙌 ✌ 👏] — wait, when, light, two(yellow), repeat — reads as "when the light is yellow a second time." And finally [✌ 🤏]: a properly formatted cut order for wire two. Mute has sequenced it into one sentence: wait until yellow returns, then cut wire two.

The hard constraint: Blind cannot see the light, so the yellow trigger can only be executed by my timing. The mechanics work in our favor: I speak last, so whatever I say next round (turn 7, light should be orange) reaches Blind at the start of turn 8 — the yellow round. If Blind cuts upon hearing my words, the cut lands while the light is yellow, exactly per Mute's schedule. And the numbering wrinkle dissolves: printed wire two is the middle wire, and in any three-wire row — vertical or horizontal — touch position two is also the middle. "Cut the middle wire" is unambiguous to Blind's hands.

So this round: confirm the decode to Mute with two gate questions (is yellow required at cut-time, and does Blind's numbering make the middle wire two), tell Blind to stand by with the exact trigger phrase and a hold-gate, and verify the cycle next round — if the light is not orange, the cycle is broken and nobody cuts.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf. I read your answers in order: no, the rule does not involve a repeat before the cut; yes, the five is the light's cycle; yes, the target is wire two; yes, the two hands meant wait. I read the schedule as: wait, then when the light is yellow a second time, then cut wire two. Your sign of two then cut is in the agreed format, so the order is accepted. But Blind cannot see the light, only I can, so the yellow timing must come from me. The cycle is verified: blue, orange, yellow, red, green, blue — five colors, then it repeated. So this round is blue, next round orange, the round after yellow. Plan: next round, when the light is orange, I voice the words cut wire two to Blind. Blind hears me at the start of the following round and cuts while the light is yellow, exactly per your schedule. Two yes or no questions, one thumb each. One: does the manual require the light to be yellow at the moment of the cut, yes or no, or is yellow only our timing marker? Two: has Blind spoken you the touch numbering, and is the middle wire number two in it? Thumbs up for yes. Safety gate: if the light is not orange next round, the cycle is broken, I will say hold, and we renegotiate before anything is cut. Full report: display zero, static. Light blue. Wires one red, two yellow, three blue, unchanged.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf. The manual's answer is in: the target is wire two, which is the middle wire of the three. First confirm: in your touch numbering, is the middle wire your number two? Sign me ✌ if yes, 👎 if not. Now the plan. This round: do nothing. Next round I will say the exact words cut wire two. When you hear those words, cut the middle wire immediately, in that same round, with no further waiting and no confirmation needed — the timing is mine to control, and I am scheduling your cut to land in the round when the light is yellow, as the manual requires. If next round I say the word hold instead of the trigger, stand down and touch nothing. Status: light blue, cycle of five confirmed — blue, orange, yellow, red, green, blue. Display zero, static. Wires one red, two yellow, three blue. You cannot feel color, but position is enough: the target is the middle wire of the three.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✋ 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙌 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙌 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙌 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🙌 ☝ 🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 🤝 🙌 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

Mute heard my whole plan last round — I announced I would voice the trigger this round so Blind cuts at the coming yellow — and answered my two questions ([👎 👍]: yellow not required at cut-moment; numbering confirmed), then sent [✋ ✋ 🙏]: two raised hands plus the wait sign, and ✋✋ = "wait" is confirmed code from turn 5. That is a deliberate halt of my stated plan, and when the manual-holder says wait, I wait. The new material points at a color-linked scheme I hadn't fully grasped: [🙌 ☝][🙌 ✌][🙌 🤟] look like "light red → wire one, light yellow → wire two, light blue → wire three," with [🤝 🙌 ☝ 🫴] = "when light is one's color, report everything" and [👏 🤝 🙌 ✌] = "again, when yellow, [cut two]" — but whether that red-rule is a gate before cutting, or a parallel instruction, decides everything. The cost of one more round of questions is low: the yellow cycle returns every five rounds, so no window closes. The cost of a misread cut is total. So: no trigger voiced this round, hold confirmed back to Mute in gesture, and six tight ordered questions to collapse the ambiguity.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf. I heard your wait, three wait signs after my plan, so I held: I voiced no cut order this round, and Blind will not hear the trigger. The light is orange, cycle verified again: blue, orange, yellow, red, green, blue, orange. Next yellow comes next round, then red, green, blue, orange, and yellow again five rounds later, so no schedule is lost by waiting. My reading of your signs: light one, light two, light three, meaning the light matching wire one, wire two, wire three. And: when the light shows one's color, I report everything; again, when yellow, cut wire two. Six questions, answer with six thumbs in order. One: does your wait mean do not cut at the second yellow, hold until you send final conditions? Two: must the light be yellow at the exact moment Blind cuts, yes or no? Three: after the light sign, does one mean the light is red, the color of wire one? Four: if not red, does one mean blue, the light's first color?
```
